title: Discographies of Morton and others
summary: Errors in discographies of Morton recordings, Cusack and Jepsen, and the difficulty of discographies.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I notice in here, there's a notation. Spikes, that's it. One record by Jelly Roll Morton's Stomp Kings, recorded in Chicago on April 1924, Steady Roll, issued on Paramount and other labels, issued on Riverside. According to Thomas Cusack's Jelly Roll Morton discography, these two titles are without jelly. Nevertheless, the Riverside Record Company has included them as Morton items in their History of Jazz series. My personal opinion, and also that of Martin Williams, is that at least Steady Roll is without Morton.

Oh, yeah. Steady Roll is not in the History of Jazz at Riverside. That's an error. Oh, it is not? No. There is a listing. It's Big Fat Hand. And they list the number of Steady Roll, but I've checked it with the other Big Fat Hand. And that's what it is. It's not Steady Roll at all. I don't have Steady Roll. I don't know what it is. Well, now, this is... But I think it's unlikely that Morton's on it. I think they're probably right.
Cusack was an Irishman. Did he come over here and do his research? According to what I...
According to what I heard, he did a very good job.
Now, this discography is on Jelly Roll, Martin, Volume 1, period 1922 to 29. I've got both of them.
That's Jorgen Grunet-Jepson. Jepson. He's done a lot of them. He did Armstrong, and he's very good. Oh, yeah. I don't think he's perfect. None of them are. But I think he's very good.

Well, Moses, I don't know how they do what they do. Years ago, I decided that those things were impossible tasks, not on Jelly Roll, because his is limited now. It has been for 20-odd years. But on these people that keep on, for instance, Duke Ellington, whoever could get out a discography on him, keeps on coming. And Blackstone in New Orleans, he went half crazy and had to quit, I think.
